concept: A silhouetted figure standing at a crossroads where multiple shadowy paths diverge into darkness, with surveillance camera eyes hovering above, weapons silhouettes crossing in the background, and storm clouds gathering at the horizon. The figure appears torn between directions, caught in overlapping spotlights. Low-angle composition, noir aesthetic, heavy contrast between dark grays and deep blues, geometric and angular forms.
explanation: Today's news is dominated by betrayal, institutional instability, and gathering external threats: soldiers spying for adversaries, political figures evading accountability, and climate catastrophe looming. The image captures the sense of a world watched, fractured, and caught between competing forces—whether geopolitical (Iran, Russia), environmental (El Niño), or domestic (political fracture in multiple nations). The crossroads represents the uncertainty and competing pull of these crises.

headlines.title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
headlines.summary: The US Department of Justice says the men were involved in a string of plots, including a major incident near the UK airbase that is used by US armed forces.

headlines.title: US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK
headlines.summary: The 41-year-old senior soldier is accused of national security offences and is being questioned in London.

headlines.title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, for now
headlines.summary: Trump welcomes the outcome, praising Hegseth as a "Great American Patriot", but Democrats can try again next year.

headlines.title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor
headlines.summary: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.

headlines.title: 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted
headlines.summary: Forecasters warn that this year's El Niño could be one of the strongest on record, with heavy rain and flooding in Kenya.

headlines.title: Headquarters of Haitian gang destroyed, El Salvador's president says
headlines.summary: The infamous 400 Mawozo gang was targeted by the El Salvador military which has deployed thousands of troops to combat Haiti's gang violence crisis.

headlines.title: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
headlines.summary: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.

headlines.title: Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch, arguing it would cast shadow on JFK's grave
headlines.summary: Nine members of the political dynasty say the 250ft structure would cast a shadow on gravesites.

headlines.title: Violence erupts in Bangladesh as ousted PM's supporters stage protest
headlines.summary: Supporters of Sheikh Hasina want her to return from exile in India.

headlines.title: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
headlines.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.

headlines.title: Spain's king and queen attend memorial service for rail crash victims
headlines.summary: Sixty-nine people died in the collision near Toledo two weeks ago and 28 are still in hospital.

headlines.title: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
headlines.summary: Najib Razak was convicted for his role in the billion-dollar scandal involving the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund.
